NovaBiotech Inc. - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaBiotech Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during the Q&A, press star then one on your telephone keypad. There will be an opportunity to ask a follow-up question by pressing star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson, Vice President of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NovaBiotech's financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Rachel Kim, Chief Medical Officer; Dr. Ben Patel, Chief Scientific Officer; Lisa Moreno, Head of Commercial; and Mark Ellis, Head of Manufacturing.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, CEO of NovaBiotech.

Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. NovaBiotech delivered a strong performance in the third quarter, driven by robust sales growth from our high-margin blockbusters like NovaCure, our leading PD-1 inhibitor, and meaningful progress across our late-stage pipeline. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities, including pipeline acceleration in oncology and rare diseases, commercial scaling in high-growth markets, and operational efficiencies through innovative technologies.

Today, I will provide an overview of our performance and strategic initiatives. We've seen exceptional cash flow generation underscoring our financial resilience, advanced clinical trial progressions with key data readouts and regulatory milestones, secured important regulatory approvals and label expansions, refined our strategic priorities with a clear outlook, prioritized R&D investments in high-ROI areas, managed our patent cliff exposure through proactive life cycle strategies, and improved gross margin trends via manufacturing efficiencies. We are particularly excited about NovaLink, our next-gen bispecific antibody, and its potential to capture significant share in solid tumors, projecting multibillion-dollar peak sales.

Now, I will turn the call over to John Ramirez, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

John Ramirez, CFO:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a solid third quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $4.8 billion, an increase of 16% compared to the same period last year. This increase was primarily driven by strong uptake of NovaCure following its U.S. label expansion into frontline NSCLC, robust demand for our BioShield vaccine franchise in emerging markets, and initial contributions from recently launched assets like NovaCheck-301.

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $820 million, or $1.52 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $980 million, or $1.82 per share.

Our operating expenses were $2.6 billion, reflecting continued investments in R&D to support our expansive pipeline, alongside targeted SG&A for commercial launches. We continue to invest heavily in R&D, with priorities centered on oncology, cardiometabolic, and gene therapies. Our cash position remains strong at $6.2 billion.

Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. I'll now turn to our Q3 cash flow and balance sheet highlights, which underscore the resilience and strategic positioning of NovaBiotech's financial profile amid a dynamic pharma landscape. Our business model—anchored by high-margin blockbusters like NovaCure, generating over $1.2 billion in quarterly net sales—and a robust late-stage pipeline continues to drive superior cash generation.

Starting with operating cash flow, we delivered $825 million in the quarter, up 22% year-over-year and 18% sequentially from Q2. This marks our ninth straight quarter of double-digit operating cash flow growth, reflecting the full-quarter benefit from NovaCure's U.S. label expansion into frontline NSCLC, which boosted net product sales by 28% in that segment alone. Excluding a $50 million one-time refund from a legacy ANDA settlement—similar to those we've seen across the industry with peers like Pfizer—we still grew adjusted operating cash flow 19% YoY. Key drivers include optimized days sales outstanding at 52 days, down from 58 last year, thanks to enhanced rebate management under the Inflation Reduction Act, and inventory turns improving to 4.8x from 4.2x, as we streamlined our API supply chain post our $200 million manufacturing reshoring initiative in North Carolina.

Free cash flow came in at $510 million, a 25% YoY increase, after $315 million in capital expenditures—within our full-year guidance of $1.2 to $1.4 billion. Capex was weighted toward high-ROI projects: 40% to expanding our sterile fill-finish capacity for NovaLink ahead of its anticipated 2025 BLA filing; 30% to digital twins and AI-optimized bioreactor tech at our Singapore hub to accelerate cell therapy scale-up; and the balance to sustainability upgrades, including ESG-compliant wastewater systems to meet EU Green Deal standards. This positions us to support 20-25% volume growth in our biologics portfolio without proportional cost inflation.

On the balance sheet, we ended the quarter with $5.8 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments—a $450 million increase from Q2—bringing our net cash position to $1.9 billion after $3.9 billion in total debt. Our investment-grade balance sheet remains fortress-like, with a net debt-to-EBITDA ratio of 0.8x, down from 1.1x a year ago, and liquidity of $7.2 billion including our undrawn $1.5 billion revolving credit facility. Current assets stood at $8.1 billion against $3.2 billion in current liabilities, yielding a current ratio of 2.5x and quick ratio of 2.1x—well above the industry median of 1.8x per Evaluate Pharma benchmarks.

Working capital efficiency improved markedly: net working capital as a percentage of revenue dipped to 18% from 22% YoY, driven by a 15% reduction in receivables through AI-powered collections analytics and just-in-time inventory for BioShield, which saw a 35% sales surge in EM Asia post-monkeypox variant approvals. We also repurchased $300 million in shares under our $2 billion program—now $1.1 billion remaining—and paid $150 million in dividends, affirming our commitment to shareholder returns while investing $950 million in R&D this quarter alone, up 12% YoY.

Regionally, U.S. cash flows were stellar at $550 million, or 67% of total, fueled by NovaCure's 45% share in the IO market, outpacing Keytruda's growth per IQVIA data, despite IRA price caps. Europe contributed $180 million, up 30% YoY on NovaCure's EMA frontline approval and ex-U.S. BioShield tenders, though tempered by launch stocking normalization. Emerging markets added $95 million, a standout 40% YoY jump from partnerships like our co-promotion deal with CSPC in China for NovaCure generics offset, and Brazil's Fiocruz for BioShield local production—mirroring Moderna's mRNA playbook but with lower COGS at 22%.

Strategically, these highlights enable us to navigate headwinds like the impending 2026 patent expiry on our TNF legacy drug, ZenoBlock—where we've already carved out $500 million in annual savings via our "PharmaFit 2.0" program, blending zero-based budgeting with robotic process automation for clinical trial matching. We're deploying $1 billion from our cash pile into bolt-on M&A, including the recent $650 million acquisition of a CRISPR gene-editing platform from a boutique biotech, accelerating our hemophilia A candidate to Phase 3. Looking forward, we reaffirm our full-year free cash flow guidance of $2.0 to $2.2 billion, positioning us to fund 10+ Phase 3 readouts in 2025, including NovaLink in solid tumors, while maintaining a dividend payout ratio below 30%.

Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. I'll now turn to our gross margin performance and the key drivers behind our manufacturing efficiency gains, which continue to be a cornerstone of our profitability profile here at NovaBiotech. In the pharma/biotech space, gross margins are a critical leading indicator of operational leverage, especially as we scale commercial volumes for our core portfolio—including NovaCure, NovaSlim-45, and NovaCheck-301.

For Q3, we delivered a GAAP gross margin of 78.5%, up 320 basis points year-over-year from 75.3% and 110 basis points sequentially from Q2's 77.4%. On a non-GAAP basis, excluding certain milestone royalties and one-time inventory write-offs related to our legacy CAR-T program, margins expanded to 81.2%, marking our strongest quarterly performance in two years. This puts us solidly on track for our full-year 2024 guidance of 79% to 81% GAAP gross margins, implying roughly 400 to 500 basis points of YoY expansion at the midpoint.

Volume mix contributed about 150 basis points of expansion. NovaCure saw U.S. volumes grow 18% YoY, driven by label expansions into adjuvant settings. This scale diluted fixed manufacturing costs. Our biosimilar portfolio—now 15% of revenues—provided a margin floor in the low 60s, offsetting ex-U.S. pricing pressure.

Raw material costs rose 4-6% YoY due to API inflation, particularly for plasmid DNA and cell culture media, but we offset this through efficiency initiatives driving 250 basis points of accretion. We've achieved a 12% YoY improvement in bioreactor yields for NovaCure at our Devens, Massachusetts site via Process Analytical Technology and AI-optimized fed-batch strategies—reducing COGS per gram by 15%, below $250. For small molecules like NovaSlim-45, continuous manufacturing at Singapore cut cycle times from 120 to 45 days, boosting throughput 30%.

Regionally, U.S. operations delivered 82% margins benefiting from 45Q tax credits; Europe at 79% via Athlone, Ireland; Asia-Pacific at 85% post-$450 million expansion, with reduced China reliance to under 10%. Ahead, $300 million in investments will drive margins to mid-80s: single-use bioreactors, digital twins, and vertical integration. Risks include IRA clawbacks and biosimilar erosion, but we're positioned for 200+ basis points annual tailwind.

Thank you, Alex. I'll now address our R&D expense and pipeline investment priorities, which remain the cornerstone of NovaBiotech's long-term value creation. For Q3 2024, total R&D expense was $1.28 billion, up 14% YoY from $1.12 billion, and 5% sequentially, equating to 28% of quarterly revenue, in line with 25-30% full-year guidance. Excluding a $85 million charge for winding down an early-stage fibrosis program, core growth was 11% YoY.

Discovery and preclinical took 22% or $282 million, up 20% for bispecifics and PROTACs. Clinical-stage was 65% or $832 million, with Phase 3 at 42% for assets like PNX-450 BTK degrader; early clinical 23% for obesity expansion. Manufacturing/regulatory 13% or $166 million for mRNA scaling.

Our $5.2 billion full-year guidance prioritizes oncology (45%), cardiometabolic (25%), gene therapy (20%). In oncology, $1.1 billion for ADCs like PNX-678 HER2-targeted entering Phase 3, with WuXi partnership. Cardiometabolic $650 million for PNX-290 GLP-1/GIP with Phase 2b data Q4. Gene therapy $400 million for PNX-GT1 AAV9 for DMD.

Efficiency gains from AI/ML cut hit-to-lead 30%; base editing for ALS. U.S. 55% spend, Europe 25%, Asia 20%. Portfolio has 12 readouts, $15 billion peak potential; $8.2 billion cash runway to 2027.

Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. As we review our Q3 results, I'd like to dive into our patent cliff exposure and life cycle management strategies. Approximately 38% of 2024 revenue—or $5.4 billion—is tied to products facing expiry 2026-2030. Aethercept, our anti-TNF biologic akin to Humira, generated $4.1 billion in 2023 U.S. sales; core patents expire 2026, with 75-85% erosion projected. Oncolix PD-1 franchise $2.8 billion at risk 2029; HepaGuard $700 million 2027. Base case $3.8-4.2 billion headwind, U.S. 65%, EU mid-2027, China wildcard.

We've invested $1.2 billion in LCM for 45-55% mitigation. Label expansions: five sNDAs for Aethercept including pediatric UC; Oncolix nine Phase 3s adding $1.5 billion. Formulation: Aethercept SC BLA Q4 2024 to 2032. Biosimilar defense: own launch 2027 clawing 10-15%. Pipeline: eight late-stage, bispecifics/ADCs $5.5 billion peak, AI cuts timelines 40%.

LCM NPV $6.2 billion, ROIC >25%. Guidance: 2024 revenue 8-10% to $14.8-15.1 billion, 2026-2030 CAGR 5-7%.

Thank you, John. Now, turning to regulatory approvals and label expansions. We've outperformed with targeted strategies. Full FDA approval of NovaCheck-301 bispecific for first-line high PD-L1 NSCLC, two months early July 15th, Priority Review; 28% PFS, 22% OS benefit vs. pembro+chemo. Companion diagnostic approved; US launch 15% share, $450 million peak 2026.

sNDA for NovaSlim-45 into adolescents 12-17 obesity/T2D; 18.5% weight loss Phase 3b, TAM +25%. EU Q4, China $300 million. Japan PMDA NovaCheck-301 Sakigake six months; $4 billion market 10% share. NovaT-19 CAR-T FL expansion; ORR 85% CR 65%, Takeda partner $200 million peak.

"LabelMax" with AI biomarkers, RWE; four expansions YTD vs. BMS two. Five PDUFA H2 including CV outcomes. These bolster 18% EBITDA, M&A optionality.

For the full year, we are updating our guidance to total revenue of $19.0 to $19.5 billion, up 15-18% at midpoint; adjusted EPS $7.20 to $7.50.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Rachel Kim, our Chief Medical Officer, to discuss our clinical programs.

Dr. Rachel Kim, Chief Medical Officer:
Thank you, John. We are very pleased with the progress of our clinical trials. Specifically, our flagship NB-101 next-gen ADC for HER2-low breast cancer met Phase 3 NOVEL-3 primary PFS endpoint: 14.2 vs. 9.1 months HR 0.64 p<0.0001, ORR 52% CR 18%; BLA year-end 2024, EMA Q1 2025, China via Innovent.

NB-202 CRISPR CAR-T for RRMM dosed first Phase 2 EXCEL-202 patient; Phase 1 ORR 78% CRR 52%, CRS 14%; RMAT designation, interim Q4 2025. NB-303 mRNA RSV Phase 2 full enrollment, >90% seroconversion; pediatric extension, Orphan status.

Regulatory: Breakthrough for NB-202, three Type B meetings, China NMPA Q2 2025. R&D burn $185 million, 3.5-year runway. These de-risk NB-101 BLA, NB-202 data 2025.

We expect to report multiple Phase 3 readouts and filings next year.

Next, Dr. Ben Patel will provide an update on our research pipeline.

Dr. Ben Patel, Chief Scientific Officer:
Thank you, Dr. Kim. We are making significant strides in our early-stage research, advancing platforms in bispecific antibodies, PROTACs, and gene editing. Key advancements include AI-optimized discovery yielding novel NMEs for NAFLD obesity and radiopharmas for prostate cancer, plus AAV enhancements for rare diseases. Our ApexAI platform has reduced timelines 40%, with three preclinical noms and partnerships like CRISPR Therapeutics. We're focused on high-barrier modalities to support pipeline infilling and hedge risks.

Now I'll turn the call over to Lisa Moreno, Head of Commercial, to discuss product sales and marketing.

Lisa Moreno, Head of Commercial:
Thank you, Dr. Patel. Our sales performance this quarter was outstanding, with oncology franchise up 18% to $2.1 billion, NovaCure capturing 45% IO share per IQVIA. U.S. 62% revenue, China ramp 45% QoQ via Sinopharm, Europe 12% share APX-201 BTK. Marketing campaigns effective in patient assistance reducing costs 40%, tenders $150 million EM. Biosimilar stabilization at $800 million run-rate.

Finally, Mark Ellis will discuss our manufacturing operations.

Mark Ellis, Head of Manufacturing:
Thank you, Lisa. Our manufacturing operations are running smoothly, with capacity expansions supporting 20-25% biologics growth. Efficiency up via PAT, continuous flow, bioreactor yields 12%, cycle times halved. Diversified: U.S. 55%, Europe 40%, Asia 25% at 85% margins. Key priorities: single-use tech, digital twins, sustainability for net-zero 2030, $1.2 billion CapEx funded internally. Supply chain derisked, ESG compliance.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Alex.

Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you, Mark. In closing my opening remarks, let me highlight our strategic priorities and outlook. We're focused on three pillars: pipeline acceleration with oncology/rare diseases leading—APX-301 22% NSCLC share, three late-stage readouts H1 2025; commercial scale, U.S. powerhouse but China to 20% by 2027, Europe/Japan expansion; innovation via $450 million ApexAI cutting timelines 40%, M&A like $1.2 billion RallyBio. FY2024 revenue $5.4-5.6 billion 16-19% growth, 2025 20-23% to $6.7-7.0 billion, FCF >$2 billion, dividend hike. Primed for mid-teens CAGR.

Thank you, team. We will now open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, instructions for the Q&A. Our first question comes from Jane Doe with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Jane Doe, Goldman Sachs:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On the patent cliff, can you elaborate on mitigation for Aethercept and expected erosion curve?

John Ramirez, CFO:
Thanks, Jane. As detailed, 75-85% U.S. erosion post-2026, but LCM including five sNDAs, SC formulation to 2032, own biosimilar clawback 10-15%, and pipeline infills reduce net risk to $2.1-2.4 billion. ROIC >25%, confident in 5-7% CAGR post-cliff.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Chen, JPMorgan:
Great, thanks. Thoughts on NB-101 BLA timeline and China partnership impact?

Dr. Rachel Kim, Chief Medical Officer:
Thanks, Mike. NOVEL-3 data robust, rolling BLA year-end under RTOR, EMA Q1 2025. Innovent handles 25% enrollment, de-risks $15 billion APAC HER2 market.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Sarah Lee, Morgan Stanley:
On gross margins, how sustainable is 81% non-GAAP, any CapEx details?

Mark Ellis, Head of Manufacturing:
Sarah, volume mix and efficiencies like 12% yield gains drive sustainability to mid-80s. $300 million next-gen single-use, digital twins; fully funded, 200 bps annual tailwind despite API inflation.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Baker with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Tom Baker, Barclays:
Quick one on R&D priorities—breakdown for oncology vs. obesity?

John Ramirez, CFO:
Tom, oncology 45% $1.1 billion for ADCs like PNX-678; cardiometabolic 25% $650 million PNX-290 Phase 2b Q4 18% loss. High IRR >15%, AI efficiencies offsetting inflation.

Operator:
Our final question from Emily Ross with Citi. Please go ahead.

Emily Ross, Citi:
Regulatory pipeline—any updates on NovaSlim-45 CV label?

John Ramirez, CFO:
Emily, on track H2 PDUFA, potential $1 billion kicker akin SGLT2; four expansions YTD, five more ahead bolstering growth.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time.

Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Thompson, Vice President of Investor Relations:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NovaBiotech Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
